points: You call every ball that lands on your side. You do not call balls on their side.
Do not call a ball out before it has bounced.
Any part of the ball touching any part of the line is good. A ball 99% out is 100% in.
A ball you cannot call out is good. There is no let for a ball you did not see.
Doubt goes to the opponent, always. This is a duty, not a courtesy.
If one partner says out and the other says good, the ball is good.
Calls must be prompt, and out calls must be heard or seen.
If you called out and then are not sure, you must reverse. The point goes to your opponent and is not replayed.
You may ask your opponent about a call that ended the point. If they give a definite opinion, you must accept it.
Except on a first serve, you can call your own ball out when you clearly see it out.

questions.q: A ball lands close to the line on your opponent's side. Whose call is it?
options: Theirs. You do not call balls on their side
Yours, if you had the better view
Either side can call it
Whoever speaks first
questions.why: You call every ball landing on your side. You do not call balls on their side.

questions.q: The ball catches the very outside edge of the line. What is the call?
options: Good
Out, because most of the ball was outside
Replay the point
Out, if both partners agree
questions.why: Any part of the ball touching any part of the line is good. A ball 99% out is 100% in.

questions.q: A ball lands near your baseline, and you did not see where it landed. What is the call?
options: Good
Play a let
Out, if it felt long
Ask someone watching
questions.why: A ball you cannot call out is good. There is no third option. Not seeing it means it was good.

questions.q: You are fairly sure the ball was out, but not certain. What is the call?
options: Good. Doubt goes to the opponent
Out. Fairly sure is enough
Play a let
Offer to split the next two points
questions.why: Doubt goes to the opponent, always. This is a duty, not a courtesy.

questions.q: In doubles, you call a ball out and your partner says it was good. What is the call?
options: Good
Out. The closer player decides
Replay the point
Out. The first call stands
questions.why: If one partner says out and the other says good, the ball is good.

questions.q: A lob is still in the air and is clearly going long. Can you call it out now?
options: No. Wait until it has bounced
Yes, if it is clearly going long
Yes, if you stand behind the baseline
Yes, if your partner agrees
questions.why: Do not call a ball out before it has bounced on your side of the court.

questions.q: How soon must you make an out call?
options: At once: before your return goes out of play or the opponent can play it
Any time before the next point starts
After you see how your own return turns out
Before the end of the game
questions.why: Calls must be prompt: before your return goes out of play, or before your opponent has a chance to play your return.

questions.q: How must you make an out call?
options: So the opponent can hear it or see it
Just stop playing. That is enough
Only if the opponent asks
By telling your partner quietly
questions.why: Out calls must be heard or seen. Your opponent is entitled to a signal.

questions.q: You call a ball out. A second later you think it may have been good. What now?
options: Reverse the call. The point goes to your opponent
Replay the point
The first call stands
Replay it the first time, lose the point the next time
questions.why: If you called out and then are not sure, you must reverse. The point goes to your opponent and is not replayed.

questions.q: A ball ends the point and you ask your opponent what they saw. They say they clearly saw it. What now?
options: You must accept what they say
You may still go with your own view
Replay the point
Ask their partner as well, and take two out of three
questions.why: You may ask for their opinion on a call that ended the point. If they give a definite opinion, you must accept it.

questions.q: You could not call a ball and you ask your opponent. They did not see it either. What is the call?
options: Good
Replay the point
Out
The server decides
questions.why: If neither of you has an opinion, the ball is good.

questions.q: In a rally, your own shot lands on their side and you clearly see it out. They play on. What may you do?
options: Call your own ball out and give them the point
Nothing. Only they can call it
Stop and ask for a let
Tell them after the point and replay it
questions.why: Except on a first serve, you can call your own ball out whenever you clearly see it out, asked or not.

questions.q: Your first serve looks clearly long to you, but the receiver returns it. Can you call your own first serve out?
options: No. The first serve is the one exception
Yes, the same as any other shot
Yes, if your partner saw it too
Yes, and you take a second serve
questions.why: You can call your own ball out when you clearly see it out, except on a first serve.
